These systems are frequently characterized by complex, rugged energy landscapes populated with numerous metastable states and high barriers separating them from the global optimum. In scenarios where a dynamic, problem-specific algorithm guides this process—such as in reinforcement learning or algorithmic metacontrol—the potential for failure arises if the distribution of masses converges to zero at the global mode, effectively starving the algorithm of necessary feedback. This letter establishes clear, quantitative criteria that determine the fate of such systems, differentiating between successful cases where mass converges to the global mode and divergent cases where it recedes. This research typically relies on the ac susceptibility method, which analyzes magnetic susceptibility at varying frequencies across a range of temperatures. Here, we present an integrated, high-throughput methodology utilizing Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) impedance spectroscopy to characterize magnetoelectric phonon coupling within a single apparatus from room temperature down to cryogenic ranges. , control, and decision-making frequently yield to robust methodologies utilizing stochastic optimization. These approaches typically integrate a learning phase, which gathers data about the decision landscape, with a subsequent phase that applies algorithms to minimize the true objective function. However, when the mapping between decision variables and actual objective values is corrupted by significant noise, learning phase methods must carefully balance the acquisition of informative data against high computational costs. This paper presents an algorithm implementing adaptive resampling strategies to satisfy theoretical bounds on regret within the context of bandit optimization. The research explores two distinct budget allocation frameworks: one with fixed allocation proportions and another with adaptive schemes. Beyond detailing the adaptive budgeting strategy, this study also investigates the allocation of budgets in multi-objective optimization. In addressing the noisy setting specifically for evolutionary algorithms, recommended algorithms are detailed, culminating in experimental validations that compare these approaches. Results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive budget allocation consistently outperforms standard fixed allocation schemes across various benchmark instances.

While radiologists typically integrate clinical expertise to differentiate pathological features, the susceptibility of clinicians to inter-observer variability underscores a need for more consistent support. Consequently, deep learning-based clinical decision support systems have emerged as a promising solution. In this study, we developed a novel region proposal approach to identify tumor boundaries and mitigate misclassification arising from co-occuring inflammation and atelectasis. We introduced an attention mechanism to enhance the model's capacity in selecting critical regions, alongside a multi-scale architecture designed to capture both fine-grained details and expansive contextual patterns. Along with the integration of a calibrated attention module to reduce competing signals from non-tissue structures, these components were optimized to enhance detection precision. Evaluated using the public KDDCep 2017 dataset, the proposed technique was benchmarked against established segmentation and classification frameworks. Results indicate a substantial 10.4% reduction in the error margin when combining our proposal with a fully connected neural network for the final decision layer for esophageal tumor identification within CT scans.

both spoken and written communication, multilingualism is increasingly common worldwide. This demographic shift invites new inquiries into whether learning one language facilitates the acquisition of another. Research indicates that such cross-linguistic influences occur through various mechanisms, ranging from negative effects like interference to beneficial outcomes such as facilitation. This review concentrates specifically on interference theories, with particular emphasis on the automatic retrieval of lexical entries from memory. These theories align closely with observed speech errors in bilingual speech, known as code-switching. According to standard retrieval-based interference models, increased mental representation of language A should enhance interference on language B; conversely, competitive inhibition suggests that stronger language A use should suppress interference on B. These opposing predictions find distinct patterns in code-switching data: both the positive correlation between bilingual first vocabulary and switch frequency, as well as the lack of correlation between second language proficiency and switching, appear within speech errors. The persistence of code-switching despite competitive inhibition accounts for the uncoupled variables in bilingual speech, suggesting that direct interference in multilingualism likely follows retrieval-based models. Consequently, multilingual speech errors probably emerge from the same cognitive mechanisms as bilingual code-switching.

In this study, we identify and quantify biases stemming from both intrinsic characteristics of the DMV dataset itself and the training algorithms used for captioning tasks. Specifically, we observe that both the intrinsic nature of the DMV dataset and the training protocols cause automatic image description models to underrepresent scenes depicting people of color, people with disabilities, and people engaged in activities that lack text labels. This paper investigates how the platform design of Facebook influences the sharing behaviors of ordinary users regarding fake news. The research compares the exposure of participants to misinformation across two conditions: one where they accessed content within their personalized news feeds and another where they viewed the same content in an uncurated, reverse-chronological format. Results demonstrate that sharing fake news increased substantially when participants viewed it within their algorithmically personalized feeds compared to the non-personalized listing. The authors conclude by suggesting that while personalization can amplify fake news through greater user engagement, it is not the sole factor, and additional variables warrant further research.

We introduce a stochastic programming framework designed to handle charging and uncharging decisions, route planning, and service requests, all within the context of uncertain request arrivals and discharge/charge durations. The model's bi-objective nature seeks to simultaneously minimize system costs and reduce carbon emissions. By employing a two-phase decomposition strategy, the study analyzes how private EVs influence these dual goals. Initial simulations reveal that incorporating private EVs into the system leads to substantial cost reductions and only marginal decreases in carbon emissions. Subsequent analysis focusing specifically on charging strategies demonstrates that directing private EVs toward charge stations with lower electricity tariffs is the most effective method for lowering overall expenses. Furthermore, optimizing routes to include charging stops for private vehicles significantly contributes to both objectives. The final phase explores how uncertainty in charging and discharging durations affects private EV system dynamics, finding that introducing discharging duration uncertainty has a more profound influence on both cost and emission outcomes than adding uncertainty to charging durations does.

This study investigates the influence of activity on the detection of low-mass planets using the Kepler dataset, specifically analyzing 109 Kepler targets containing confirmed planets with periods under 100 days. Conversely, in real-world uses like traffic monitoring or factory equipment detection, contexts are often restricted. Although these contexts are not explicitly defined, they can be inferred from the training images themselves. This paper defines 'context' as the specific characteristics that differentiate object detection performance across different image collections derived from different sources. We posit that context influences performance by introducing distribution discrepancies between general training data (like COCO) and narrower-scoped detection tasks. To address this, we have created 'Contextual Image Selection' (CIS), a technique that identifies images within large databases that align contextually with a given contextual profile. With access to both labeled data and general object annotations (such as COCO), our method utilizes contextual features extracted via unsupervised contrastive learning to identify and filter images sharing that same context. Furthermore, we propose a framework for contextual refinement through iterative optimization that leverages both labeled and limited detection images. Contextual image selection is an end-to-end method capable of enhancing object detection performance on contexts with sparse data (containing fewer than 100 images per category). Experimental results indicate that contexts contextual image selection can substantially outperform standard methods (such as COCO) by an average margin of 3.6% mAP on contexts with fewer than 100 images per class. In the context of domain theory, this field focuses on representing computational domains—specifically those arising in programming languages—alongside the continuous functions defined over them. To overcome this limitation, we introduce Graph Neural Network with Sparsest Cut-based Convolution (GNN-SPC), a method designed to accelerate convolution by aggregating sparsest cuts. This approach partitions the neighborhood of any given node into multiple dense subgraphs, treating each as an independent convolution operation. To maximize expected revenue, we develop a revenue-optimized configuration algorithm, proving in the appendices that it achieves polynomial-time complexity. extensive simulations using both real-world and randomly generated data confirm the model's effectiveness, demonstrating that revenue-aware designs yield significantly higher earnings than performance-centric approaches, with revenue-optimized configurations delivering a 30% increase in revenue over performance-only strategies.

the mechanisms behind sudden regime changes are critical concerns in ecology, economics, and sociology. While most SR-GANs are trained on pairs of low- and high-resolution images, the scarcity of natural high-resolution data and the limited diversity of downscaling methods constrain the growth of super-resolution GANs. To overcome these bottlenecks, we introduce Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) into the style transfer super-resolution (STSR-GAN) framework for the task of unsupervised super-resolution. Our proposed approach, termed STSR-GAN with UDA, enables joint training using only high-resolution data. Specifically, we develop an improvement upon the STSR-GAN model using UDA to generate synthetic SR pairs from only real HR images. By employing reverse cycle GAN loss and a newly designed gradient adjustment mechanism, we ensure that generated super images maintain realistic textures and structural integrity. Experiments confirm that this method, when trained exclusively on high-res single images, achieves performance comparable to models trained on large SR datasets across various benchmarks. Furthermore, this UDA-enhanced framework delivers significant improvements when applied to super-resolution of textures and images in real-world scenarios.

This document presents a detailed examination of the numerical characteristics of these calculation methods, with a specific focus on the standard shot-noise approximation. Our analysis reveals that the conventional grid-based approach, which utilizes a calculation mesh, suffers from significant systematic biases when determining the potential at low coordinates relative to the center of the calculation domain. These issues are addressed by the implementation of several optimized algorithms, including the Fast Multipole Method (FMM) and a novel strategy referred to as Boundary FMM. These techniques establish a robust framework for evaluating the shot-noise approximation, ensuring reliable results for experimental applications. Additionally, these methods have facilitated the systematic investigation of calculation parameters, offering practical insights into the relationship between simulation resolution, convergence behavior, and detector sensitivity within current and upcoming experiments.
